Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - testEncodingInputStream iterates over a set of archive types. For each, it builds an ArchiveInputStream via ArchiveStreamFactory and then reads a private “encoding”-related field from the created stream by reflection. It asserts that the value matches the expected encoding supplied to the factory.

- How ArchiveStreamFactory is supposed to propagate encoding:
  - ArchiveStreamFactory stores the effective encoding in entryEncoding.
    - ArchiveStreamFactory(String encoding) sets both encoding and entryEncoding to the provided value.
    - setEntryEncoding only sets entryEncoding (and throws if encoding was set via constructor).
  - When creating ArchiveInputStreams, the factory should pass entryEncoding into the corresponding stream constructors that accept an encoding.

- What the code actually does:
  - In the name-based factory method createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream):
    - For ARJ, CPIO, DUMP, JAR, TAR, ZIP: it correctly checks entryEncoding and passes it to the respective XxxArchiveInputStream constructors when not null, otherwise uses the no-arg-encoding constructors. This path is consistent.

  - In the auto-detect factory method createArchiveInputStream(InputStream):
    - ZIP, JAR, CPIO: correctly pass entryEncoding when not null.
    - ARJ: always uses new ArjArchiveInputStream(in) and never passes entryEncoding. This drops the encoding completely for ARJ in auto-detection.
    - DUMP: unconditionally calls new DumpArchiveInputStream(in, entryEncoding). If entryEncoding is null, this still invokes the two-arg constructor with null instead of using the no-arg-encoding constructor, which may result in null encoding being set rather than the intended default.
    - TAR (primary match): correctly returns new TarArchiveInputStream(in, entryEncoding).
    - TAR (fallback path after checksum verification): incorrectly uses new TarArchiveInputStream(in, encoding) instead of entryEncoding. If the encoding was set via setEntryEncoding (i.e., encoding is null), this mistakenly passes null and loses the configured value.

- Why the test fails:
  - The test expects the encoding provided to ArchiveStreamFactory to be reflected in the created ArchiveInputStream’s internal encoding field.
  - There are code paths in the auto-detect createArchiveInputStream(InputStream) that either:
    - Don’t pass any encoding at all (ARJ), or
    - Use the wrong field (encoding instead of entryEncoding for TAR fallback), or
    - Pass a null encoding explicitly (DUMP) instead of choosing the constructor that uses the default.
  - Depending on which archive is created and how the factory’s encoding was configured (constructor vs setEntryEncoding), the created stream ends up with a null/default encoding. The reflective check then finds a mismatch with the expected encoding, incrementing the failure counter.

- Alignment with the bug report:
  - The bug report mentions failures to pass through encoding for ArjArchiveInputStream, CpioArchiveInputStream, DumpArchiveInputStream, JarArchiveInputStream, and JarArchiveOutputStream.
  - In the input-stream side:
    - ARJ: confirmed omission in auto-detect.
    - TAR (not listed in report) has a wrong-field usage in the fallback path; this is an additional inconsistency that can also manifest.
    - DUMP: potential null-propagation issue.
    - JAR and CPIO: name-based and auto-detect paths are correct for input streams; the report’s inclusion likely refers to other creation paths or historical inconsistency.
  - On the output-stream side (not covered by the shown test), there are likely similar omissions when creating JarArchiveOutputStream.

Root cause:
- Inconsistent and incorrect propagation of the effective encoding from ArchiveStreamFactory to the concrete archive stream constructors in the auto-detect path:
  - Missing propagation for ARJ.
  - Using encoding instead of entryEncoding for TAR fallback.
  - Passing null explicitly for DUMP rather than using the constructor that applies a default.

This inconsistency causes some created ArchiveInputStream instances to have no encoding set (or the wrong one), making the test’s field comparison fail.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
